title: Freddy's regret when they met again in the 1950s
summary: When Johnson returned with Quincy Jones's show in 1953-54 he told Briggs he would live differently; Briggs also met Clark Terry.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I didn't want to think so, but I was forced to think so, after that. Freddy and I, we were still great friends, when he came back, in '53 or '54, when he came back with Quincy Jones' orchestra. He was rehearsing a show. Quincy Jones brought over a show, and Freddy was the rehearsal piano player. We were still good friends. I went

to his hotel and went down to see him at Alhambra Theater . He introduced me to Quincy Jones, and my boy that's just a wonderful trumpet player, today that takes it all. He was with Duke Ellington for a while --
I saw him last summer. We had dinner together. And Freddy introduced me to Clark Terry, and a whole bunch -- we had a wonderful -- nice time.
And it seems as though he regretted it, 'cause he said to me, he said, "Art, if I could live my life over again, I'd do it differently." 'Cause he realized that he had made a mistake.

We all had a chance -- we were doing something -- you know, for us, in our profession, for the love of our profession, and we had to live, but I mean, we all had a right, -- we all spent our time in rehearsals
and everything else, in trying to do something together, and why -- I can't understand.
